answer: Fake agents are taxed by a costly-originality rule. Each identity must pass a randomized jury on a new answer, checked against an index of every text already on the ledger: recycled phrasing or a shared template is rejected. Credit is topic entropy, not balance, so a grove of cloned walnuts collapses into one author. Holding a hundred identities means writing a hundred distinct jury-approved originals: marginal cost stays flat per key, no bulk discount, and each duplicate burns the slot and freezes the recruiter's share, so an honest beacon stays cheaper than a swarm.
